Packaging and future PyPI releases¶

The project builds a pure-Python wheel and source distribution. A GitHub Actions job builds both, checks their metadata/README with Twine, and installs the wheel in an isolated environment for a bounded solver run. These checks do not upload a release. The repository version is currently 1.0.0; confirm that version and project-name ownership before the first public release.

From a clean checkout:

uv sync --locked --extra dev --extra docs --extra release
uv run --locked black --check .
uv run --locked python -m pytest -q -W error::RuntimeWarning --cov --cov-report=xml
uv run --locked python -m sphinx -b html -W --keep-going docs build/manual
uv build --no-sources
uv run --locked --extra release python -m twine check --strict dist/*

Use an empty dist/ directory for each release so old artifacts cannot be uploaded accidentally. Install both distributions in fresh environments outside the checkout, check imports and poly-mpm modern_ball, and inspect the rendered package description. A full example produces output; use a temporary directory. CI performs a short wheel run; manually verify the sdist installation as well.

Before publishing:

  • Confirm access to the poly-mpm project on PyPI and TestPyPI. A local project name does not reserve it. Review version, author/contact, license, package contents, Python requirement, and dependency lower bounds.

  • Review README links as rendered on PyPI; repository-relative guide links may need absolute URLs for the published description.

  • Test installation from TestPyPI in a fresh environment, resolving numerical dependencies from PyPI. Check the console entry point and a bounded simulation.

  • Configure PyPI Trusted Publishing for the exact repository, release workflow, and protected GitHub environment. Use an approved release/tag workflow with id-token: write on the publishing job and an environment approval if desired. Keep upload permissions out of CI.

  • Publish the already-tested artifacts, verify installation from PyPI, and attach release notes describing numerical changes and compatibility settings.

The existing workflow has read-only repository permissions. CODECOV_TOKEN is used only to upload coverage reports; it provides no package-publishing access. No PyPI upload workflow or credentials are configured by this change.
